claim: A soil report from a prospective plot returns 20% active lime and a chlorosis index (IPC) of 60. Which rootstock decision does that force?
because: The site values sit inside 140 Ruggeri's published tolerance: Plantgrape (IFV/INRAE/Montpellier SupAgro) and the Pépinière Richard aptitude table both rate 140 Ru to 20% active lime and IPC 90. At 20% / IPC 60, 140 Ru is not ruled out, so option C ('110R or 140 Ruggeri') is half-viable and the soil does not 'force' 41B/Fercal. A careful examiner could defend 140 Ru on this plot. (41B is 40% / IPC 60 and Fercal 40% / IPC 120 in the same sources, so the key is right once the numbers exceed 140 Ru's limit.)
fix: Change the stem to 'A soil report from a prospective plot returns 30% active lime and a chlorosis index (IPC) of 60. Which rootstock decision does that force?' That puts the plot above 140 Ru's 20% and 110R's 17%, and still inside 41B (40%, IPC 60) and Fercal (40%, IPC 120). Keep the key at index 1.
